content.text:
You are the Niyam encoder. Update this rulebook so it matches a new government document.

The validated change set is in `.niyam/changeset.json`. It lists each change with its exact source quote, page and clause.
The source document is registered in `sources/index.yaml` as `gr-22ba2391c901dba5` (date 2024-07-01).

Do this:
1. Read CLAUDE.md (the rulebook rules), the change set, and the files of the affected scheme(s): mh.ladki_bahin.
2. Apply every change in the change set, following CLAUDE.md exactly:
   - parameter change: add a new dated value under `values:` starting 2024-07-01. Never edit or delete older values.
   - condition change: set `valid_until` on the old condition to the day before 2024-07-01, and add a new condition with the same id and `valid_from: 2024-07-01`.
   - condition removed: only set `valid_until` to the day before 2024-07-01.
   - every new value or condition gets `source` / `metadata.reference` with doc `gr-22ba2391c901dba5`, page, clause, quote (copied from the change set) and quote_en.
   - if a change needs a new person field, add it to `schema/person.yaml` with a safe default that keeps existing results unchanged.
3. Add test citizens to `tests/` for every change, dated on or after 2024-07-01: just below, at, and just above each limit, plus one case dated before 2024-07-01 proving the old rule still applies. Each case cites `GR 22ba2391c901dba5 p.<page> clause <clause>` in `source`.
4. Add an entry at the top of CHANGELOG.md (English, Hindi, Marathi) linking to the document.
5. Run `python -m niyam_rulebook test` and fix problems until it prints `0 failed` with no PROBLEM lines.
6. Do not run git. Do not edit files outside schemes/, parameters/, tests/, sources/, glossary/, schema/ and CHANGELOG.md.

Finish with a short summary of what you changed and the final test result.
I'll start by reading the rulebook rules, the change set, and the affected scheme files.

1	# Interpretation glossary: Maharashtra government resolutions
2	
3	How Niyam reads recurring legal phrases. The agent reads this file before
4	extracting or resolving, and adds an entry whenever it settles an ambiguity.
5	Each entry cites where the interpretation came from. Entries marked
6	"needs human confirmation" have not been confirmed by a person yet.
7	
8	## "पेक्षा जास्त नसावे" (should not be more than)
9	Inclusive upper limit: a value equal to the limit is allowed.
10	Source: GR 202406281814018230, clause 4(5), income "not more than Rs 2.50 lakh".
11	
12	## "पेक्षा जास्त" (more than)
13	Strict comparison: a value equal to the limit is not "more than" the limit.
14	Source: GR 202406281814018230, clauses 5(4) and 5(7).
15	
16	## "किंवा त्यापेक्षा जास्त" (or more than that)
17	Inclusive: a value equal to the limit counts.
18	
19	## "वयाची N वर्षे पूर्ण होईपर्यंत" (until N years of age are completed)
20	Niyam stores ages as completed years and treats the upper age N as eligible
21	(age N is inside the range). This matches the scheme summary in the same GR,
22	"21 ते 60 या वर्ष वयोगटातील" (in the 21 to 60 age group).
23	Status: needs human confirmation. A strict reading could end eligibility on the
24	Nth birthday.
25	
26	## "कुटुंब" (family)
27	Not yet defined in the rulebook. Niyam treats family facts (income, tax payer,
28	government job, land, vehicle) as reported by the applicant for her household.
29	
30	## Dates
31	A GR applies from its own date unless it states another start date.
32	A change to an earlier GR keeps the earlier value in history (a new dated value
33	is added; old values are never edited).
34

1	# Instructions for coding agents working in this rulebook
2	
3	This repository is the Niyam rulebook: Maharashtra welfare scheme eligibility
4	rules as tested code. Every rule must trace back to an official government
5	document. Wrong rules can stop people from receiving money they are owed.
6	
7	## Layout
8	- `schemes/<state>/<scheme>.yaml`: conditions and benefit. Every condition has `valid_from`, optional `valid_until`, and a `source` (doc, page, clause, quote, quote_en).
9	- `parameters/<state>/<scheme>/<name>.yaml`: dated values in OpenFisca format. Each value has `metadata.reference` (doc, page, clause, quote, quote_en).
10	- `tests/<state>/<scheme>.yaml`: test citizens. Each case has `date`, `person`, `expect` and `source`.
